title: Insert multiple companies at once
description:
Given the set `it_companies = {'Facebook', 'Google', 'Microsoft', 'Apple', 'IBM', 'Oracle', 'Amazon'}`: Insert multiple IT companies at once to the set it_companies.

Python-Gym adaptation: implement as `add_multiple_companies(it_companies, companies)`, where `companies` is an iterable (e.g. a list) of new company names to insert into the given set all at once, returning a SORTED list of the resulting set's contents.
hints: Adding elements one at a time with .add() would work, but sets have a method built specifically for inserting many elements at once.
Look for the set method that takes an iterable (like a list) and merges all of its items into the set in one call.
Call the set's .update() method with the companies list, then return sorted(it_companies).
expected_behavior: Inserts every item from the given iterable into the set in one call, and returns a sorted list of the updated set's contents.

hidden_tests.label: original it_companies set plus two new companies
small set plus two new items
adding an item that already exists changes nothing

explanation: set.update() merges every element of the given iterable into the set in a single call, which is more direct than looping and calling .add() repeatedly. Duplicate elements are simply ignored since a set can't hold repeats.
